label: BASIC-11 V007A
description: Interactive BASIC-11 loaded into PDP-11 memory, executing numerical and string expressions.

label: Lunar Lander
description: Lunar Lander on the VT11 vector display — the landing in progress. Use the mouse as a light pen: hover over the on-screen controls to steer and set thrust — no clicking.

label: Unix V5
description: Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie's Research Unix V5 (1974) with early C compiler, sh, and roff.

label: RT-11 v4.0
description: DEC Real-Time operating system widely deployed in laboratory instrumentation and Soviet clones.

label: RT-11 v4.0 (teletype console)
description: RT-11 booted on the Model 33 ASR teletype console — upper case only, the way the original operator saw it.

label: RT-11 v4.0 (VT52 console)
description: RT-11 interacting with the DECscope VT52 CRT terminal emulator running on canvas.

label: RSTS V06C-03
description: RSTS/E V06C-03, the timesharing system DEC sold to everybody who could not afford a mainframe — answer START at the Option: prompt.

label: XXDP (diagnostics)
description: DEC field diagnostic operating system used to test CPU instructions, memory management, and peripherals.

label: BSD 2.11
description: Berkeley Software Distribution 2.11 in full multiuser mode, featuring vi, cc, TCP/IP networking stack.

label: RT-11 Adventure
description: Colossal Cave — Will Crowther and Don Woods' original text adventure, the cave crawl that started the genre (and inspired Dungeon): it opens at the end of a road before a small brick building."

label: RT-11 Dungeon
description:
The MIT text adventure that grew into Zork — a FORTRAN IV dungeon crawl under RT-11, billed by its authors as "a game of adventure, danger and low cunning.

It starts at the boarded white house...

label: RT-11 Print Coguar
description:
Prints the classic "COUGAR" ASCII art banner page on the line printer (LP:).
Highly popular on PDP-11 systems as a continuous-feed banner page or a team mascot and a practical benchmark to test printer hardware.

label: RT-11-SPCINV
description:
VAX port for PDP-11.
As close to the original as possible...

label: RT-11-TIME52
description: The $100,000 Digital Timepiece from 1975: Why settle for a cheap wristwatch when you can track the relentless passage of time using a legendary DEC PDP-11/70 minicomputer and a VT52 DECScope terminal?
